name: Single-digit Numerative

dimensions.meaning: Specifies cardinality from zero to nine
dimensions.function: Factor, addition, determiner; most versatile numerative subclass
dimensions.distribution: All numerative positions; combine freely in compounds

1.definition: Specifies a cardinal value from zero to nine

projection.target: The digit 0 participates as the lexeme zero and can determine a plural in zero defects. One differs in selecting a singular count nominal. The single-digit class therefore does not predict uniform agreement or determiner selection.
projection.evidence: CGEL gives the cardinal distribution and Reynolds includes zero in the basic lexical inventory. The comparison separates numerical representation from grammatical number.

curious.title: The words for zero to nine
curious.summary: The single-word numbers from zero to nine can do any job a number word does, though they don't all behave alike.
curious.body: The numbers from zero to nine are single words: one, two, three and so on up to nine, plus zero. They can stand in front of a noun, multiply a bigger number, or be added to one, as in forty-two. They don't all act the same. One goes with a singular noun, while zero can go with a plural, as in zero defects. This dictionary says that being a single-digit number doesn't tell you how a word will agree or what kind of noun follows it.
curious.try: Say one apple, then zero apples. Which has a plural ending on the noun?

teacher.summary: Covers the digit words zero to nine, and why they don't all select the same kind of noun.
teacher.explain: Single-digit numeratives are the monomorphemic lexemes zero to nine. They specify cardinality and can function as a factor, as an addend or as a determiner, and they combine freely in compounds. They don't predict uniform agreement or determiner selection. Zero participates as the lexeme zero and can determine a plural (zero defects). One selects a singular count nominal. This dictionary separates the numerical representation, the digit, from grammatical number. It is provisional.
teacher.terms: Numeral, or cardinal numeral, is the traditional name. Digit refers to the written symbol 0 to 9, which this dictionary distinguishes from the lexeme.
watch_for: A learner might expect one to go with a plural noun in the way five does.
A learner might think zero must go with a singular noun, because it stands for none.
teacher.activity: Students write a noun phrase for each word from zero to nine (for example zero defects, one chapter, five dogs) and sort them by whether the noun is singular or plural.
